title: the web-server shim proof stops the listener it started on Windows, so its scratch dir can be removed
intention: the web-server shim proof's teardown ends the whole listener process tree on Windows (taskkill /T), where it ended nothing, so the scratch dir it made is removable.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: two listener.py --port 42299 processes (pids 29384 and its child 14384) outlived their dead parent 28712 and held web_server.log in ws-shim-pulse-scratch.0-28712-*, read from Win32_Process
traces_to: Law 3: the leak was measured as two orphan processes; Law 7: the sweep said so loudly, and the proof that left it is the writer to fix, not the sweep.
how: In cairn/devices/web_server/proofs/test_web_server_shim.py the finally of test_the_pulse_holds_the_port_on_the_home_only calls a small _stop_tree(pid) defined in the proof: on nt it runs taskkill /F /T /PID with a hidden window, otherwise os.killpg as now. Red-first proof cairn/devices/web_server/proofs/test_the_shim_proof_stops_what_it_started.py scans that file's source with ast: no bare os.killpg inside a finally that has no nt branch, and a taskkill call exists. No process is spawned by the new proof.

clauses.claim: the source of test_web_server_shim.py contains a taskkill tree-stop for nt and no killpg without an nt branch, where the unedited file has a bare killpg
after the shim proof runs on Windows no process of listener.py --port <its port> remains
